answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil accounts by requiring each identity to lock a scarce-token bond before requesting work. The protocol releases the bond only after verified service; an account that fails a random audit forfeits it. An attacker must fund each fabricated identity separately and risk losing its full bond, so attack costs grow with account count instead of the negligible cost of scripts. A relic receipt can carry a quill signature, and a sparrow test job can expose copied behavior before larger payouts.
